title: Azure Backup Job Failures

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `mscs:azure:audit` events with `operationName.value="*Backup*" status.value="Failed"` into `index=azure`. Confirm UC-4.2.15 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `mscs:azure:audit` traffic without `operationName.value="*Backup*" status.value="Failed"`. Confirm UC-4.2.15 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:audit` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

description: UC-4.2.15 — Azure Backup Job Failures: queries Microsoft Azure `mscs:azure:audit` for search criteria `operationName.value="*Backup*" status.value="Failed"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for fault review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Azure Backup Job Failures' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.2.15 drives critical-priority fault alerting before customer-impacting drift.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:audit`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable Activity Log or diagnostic settings for Recovery Services vault. Ingest backup job completion events. Alert on status=Failed. Dashboard job success rate by vault and policy.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:audit" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:audit" operationName.value="*Backup*" status.value="Failed"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.15_azure_backup_job_failure_15"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:audit` in `index=azure` to detect azure backup job failures. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_15_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Table (job, vault, status, time), Timeline (failed jobs), Single value (failed last 24h)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure backup job failures so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
